sections.heading: 1. Key Expressions & Sentences Reviewed (Lessons 57–63)
points: Lesson 57: "Rima munda wako zvakanaka kuti uwane goho guru." — Cultivate your field well so that you get a big harvest.
Lesson 58: "Gore rino kuchange kuine gohwo rakanaka, handiti?" — This year there will be a good harvest, won't there?
Lesson 59: "Nekuda kwekushanda nesimba, akawana mubayiro." — Because of working hard, he received a reward.
Lesson 60: "Tichasangana naamai kumusika kana tapedza kutenga miriwo." — We will meet Mother at the market when we finish buying vegetables.
Lesson 61: "Humambo hweRozvi hwaizivikanwa neuto ravo raigona kurwa hondo." — The Rozvi Empire was renowned for its army that was skilled in warfare.
Lesson 62: "Vanhu vaitengeserana nyanga dzenzou nendarama nevatorwa vaibva kure." — People traded ivory and gold with foreign merchants who came from afar.
Lesson 63: "Nhoroondo dzekare dzinotidzidzisa kwatakabva netsika dzedu semaShona." — Ancient history teaches us where we came from and our traditions as Shona people.

sections.heading: 2. Core Shona Grammar Rules Consolidated
points: Giving Commands & Polite Requests ('Rima'): Singular Command: Verb stem (-a) [Huya! / Tora!] | Polite or Plural Command: Verb stem + -i (-ai) [Huyai! / Torai!]
Talking About the Past ('rakanaka'): Recent Today Past: [nda- / wa- / ta- / va-] + verb | Earlier Past: [ndaka- / waka- / taka- / vaka-] + verb
Talking About the Past ('akawana'): Recent Today Past: [nda- / wa- / ta- / va-] + verb | Earlier Past: [ndaka- / waka- / taka- / vaka-] + verb
Talking About the Future with '-cha-' ('Tichasangana'): Subject Prefix + -cha- + Verb Stem = Future ('will') -> Ndichaenda (I will go), Vachadzoka (They will return)
Possessive Pronouns: Saying 'My', 'Your', and 'Our' ('ravo'): Noun + [Linking Prefix + -ngu (my) / -ko (your) / -ke (his/her) / -du (our) / -nyu (your polite) / -vo (their)]
Joining Words with 'ne-' ('and / with') in 'nendarama': ne- + Noun = and / with [Noun] (written as a single word, e.g., sadza nemuriwo = sadza and vegetables)

sections.heading: 3. Cultural Context & Practical Usage
points: Thorough Field Preparation ('Kurima Munda') for a Bountiful Harvest: Good farming ('kurima munda zvakanaka')—winter ploughing, adding organic compost or manure ('mupfudze'), and timely weeding ('kusakura')—is celebrated across Zimbabwe as the secret to achieving a bumper harvest ('goho guru')..

Predicting the Harvest ('Gohwo Rakanaka') & Conversational 'Handiti?': When the rains fall evenly through December and January, farmers look across green fields of waist-high maize and optimism rises for a strong harvest ('gohwo rakanaka').

Honouring Hard Work ('Kushanda Nesimba') & Academic/Work Awards ('Mubayiro'): Schools, churches, and workplaces in Zimbabwe hold annual prize-giving days to award prizes ('mubayiro') to students and workers who have distinguished themselves through diligence ('kushanda nesimba')..

Open-Air Farmer's Markets ('Musika') & Community Meeting Points: From Harare's famous Mbare Musika to Sakubva in Mutare and Renkini in Bulawayo, the 'musika' (open-air market) is both the primary source of farm-fresh vegetables ('miriwo') and a central landmark where family members arrange to meet up ('kusangana') before travelling home together..

review_exercises.prompt: Review 9 — History & Heritage: Why is Great Zimbabwe called 'Masvingo eGreat Zimbabwe'?
options: Because 'masvingo' means tall green trees
Because it is located beside the Indian Ocean
Because 'masvingo' means modern glass buildings
Because 'masvingo' means fortified dry-stone walls or enclosures
review_exercises.correct_answer: Because 'masvingo' means fortified dry-stone walls or enclosures
review_exercises.explanation: 'Masvingo' refers to the monumental stone enclosures built by ancestors of the Shona people.

review_exercises.prompt: Review 9 — Wildlife & Nature: In 'zvipembere zviviri zviri kufura uswa', what are the two rhinoceroses doing?
options: Grazing on grass
Drinking water from the river
Sleeping under a shady tree
Running across the mountain

review_exercises.prompt: Review 9 — National Flag Colours: Which five colours appear on the national flag of Zimbabwe ('mureza weZimbabwe')?
options: Blue, purple, orange, pink, and grey
Green (girinhi), yellow (yero), red (tsvuku), black (tema), and white (chena)
Only green and white
Red, blue, and gold only
review_exercises.correct_answer: Green (girinhi), yellow (yero), red (tsvuku), black (tema), and white (chena)
review_exercises.explanation: The Zimbabwean flag features horizontal stripes of green, yellow, red, and black with a white triangle bearing the Zimbabwe Bird.

review_exercises.prompt: Review 9 — Water Storage & Households: Why are Jojo tanks ('matangi emvura eJojo') placed on elevated brick or steel stands?
options: To serve as watchtowers for wildlife
To dry maize and groundnuts in the sun
To store household water and provide gravity pressure for taps
To shelter livestock during the rainy season
review_exercises.correct_answer: To store household water and provide gravity pressure for taps
review_exercises.explanation: Elevated water tanks store borehole or municipal water so households have a reliable supply.

review_exercises.prompt: Review 9 — Translate this new cumulative sentence: 'Nzvimbo iyi inoratidza nhoroondo yakakosha yevanhu vekare nemagariro avo.'
options: This place shows the important history of the ancient people and their way of life.
These mountains have many green trees and clean rivers.
The visitors took photographs of the two rhinoceroses.
We learned many Shona words, proverbs, and grammar rules.
review_exercises.correct_answer: This place shows the important history of the ancient people and their way of life.
review_exercises.explanation: 'Nzvimbo iyi inoratidza' = 'This place shows', 'nhoroondo yakakosha' = 'important history', 'yevanhu vekare nemagariro avo' = 'of the ancient people and their way of life'.
